claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantification of immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1F.

claims.claim: There is little co-labeling of CCK+ cells with SOM (6.6% overlap).
claims.source: Importantly, we found little co-labeling of CCK+ cells with either PV (Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1; 11.3% overlap, n = 308 cells total, 17 slices, 6 animals) or SOM (6.6% overlap, n = 105 cells total, 8 slices, 3 animals).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantification of immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1F.

claims.claim: CCK+ interneurons have intrinsic properties with Rin = 130 ± 13 MΩ, Vm = −68 ± 1 mV, Sag = 4.1 ± 1.0%, Adaptation = 0.81 ± 0.04, Tau = 9.1 ± 0.6 ms.
claims.source: We found both axons and dendrites in L5 of IL PFC, and intrinsic properties similar to reports in other parts of the brain (Figure 1H; Rin = 130 ± 13 MΩ, Vm = −68 ± 1 mV, Sag = 4.1 ± 1.0%, Adaptation = 0.81 ± 0.04, Tau = 9.1 ± 0.6 ms; n = 12 cells, 4 animals) (Daw et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 1H.

claims.claim: vHPC inputs evoke robust EPSCs at CCK+ interneurons, which are similar in amplitude to IT cells (CCK+/IT ratio = 0.56).
claims.source: We found that vHPC inputs evoked robust EPSCs at CCK+ interneurons, which were similar in amplitude to IT cells (Figure 2A; IT = 674 ± 102 pA, CCK+ = 413 ± 89 pA, CCK+/IT ratio = 0.56, p = 0.13; n = 9 pairs, 4 animals).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by paired electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: vHPC inputs evoke prominent EPSCs at PV+ interneurons, with comparable amplitudes at IT cells (PV+/IT ratio = 0.94).
claims.source: We also found prominent vHPC-evoked EPSCs at PV+ interneurons, with comparable amplitudes at IT cells (Figure 2B; IT = 569 ± 91 pA, PV+ = 555 ± 83 pA, PV+/IT ratio = 0.94, p = 0.82; n = 9 pairs, 4 animals).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by paired electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: vHPC inputs evoke much smaller EPSCs at SOM+ interneurons compared to IT cells (SOM+/IT ratio = 0.17).
claims.source: By contrast, vHPC inputs evoked much smaller EPSCs at SOM+ interneurons compared to IT cells (Figure 2C; IT = 421 ± 69 pA, SOM+ = 95 ± 33 pA, SOM+/IT ratio = 0.17, p = 0.004; n = 9 pairs, 4 animals).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by paired electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: All three cell types (CCK+, PV+, SOM+) receive direct vHPC inputs, with greater responses at CCK+ and PV+ interneurons.
claims.source: These findings show that all three cell types receive direct vHPC inputs, with greater responses at CCK+ and PV+ interneurons.
claims.evidence: This is a summary inference based on the electrophysiological data from Figure 2A-C.

claims.claim: Single vHPC inputs evoke APs in pairs of CCK+ and IT cells but the interneurons show a higher probability of firing (IT = 0.32 ± 0.15, CCK+ = 0.84 ± 0.11, p = 0.03).
claims.source: We found that single vHPC inputs evoked APs in pairs of CCK+ and IT cells but the interneurons showed a higher probability of firing (Figure 2D; AP probability: IT = 0.32 ± 0.15, CCK+ = 0.84 ± 0.11, p = 0.03; n = 9 pairs, 4 animals).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by current-clamp recordings shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: vHPC inputs preferentially activate PV+ over IT cells (IT = 0.06 ± 0.06, PV+ = 0.65 ± 0.17, p = 0.04).
claims.source: Similarly, we observed that vHPC inputs also preferentially activate PV+ over IT cells (Figure 2E; AP probability: IT = 0.06 ± 0.06, PV+ = 0.65 ± 0.17, p = 0.04; n = 8 pairs, 4 animals).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by current-clamp recordings shown in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: SOM+ interneurons remain unresponsive to vHPC inputs, even when using higher light intensities that activate IT cells (IT = 0.81 ± 0.12, SOM+ = 0.13 ± 0.06, p = 0.01).
claims.source: By contrast, SOM+ interneurons remained unresponsive to vHPC inputs, even when using higher light intensities that were able to activate IT cells (Figure 2F; AP probability: IT = 0.81 ± 0.12, SOM+ = 0.13 ± 0.06, p = 0.01; n = 7 pairs, 3 animals).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by current-clamp recordings shown in Figure 2F.

claims.claim: CCK+ and PV+ interneurons are engaged by vHPC inputs and mediate feed-forward inhibition.
claims.source: These results established a hierarchy for activation, suggesting CCK+ and PV+ interneurons are engaged by vHPC inputs and mediate feed-forward inhibition.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the action potential probability data from Figure 2.

claims.claim: EPSCs at CCK+ interneurons strongly depress over the course of stimulus trains (EPSC2 / EPSC1: CCK+ = 0.82 ± 0.06).
claims.source: We observed that EPSCs at CCK+ and PV+ interneurons strongly depress over the course of stimulus trains (Figure 3A & B; EPSC2 / EPSC1: CCK+ = 0.82 ± 0.06; n = 6 cells, 3 animals; PV+ = 0.88 ± 0.06; n = 7 cells, 3 animals).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings during repetitive stimulation shown in Figure 3A-B.

claims.claim: EPSCs at PV+ interneurons strongly depress over the course of stimulus trains (EPSC2 / EPSC1: PV+ = 0.88 ± 0.06).
claims.source: We observed that EPSCs at CCK+ and PV+ interneurons strongly depress over the course of stimulus trains (Figure 3A & B; EPSC2 / EPSC1: CCK+ = 0.82 ± 0.06; n = 6 cells, 3 animals; PV+ = 0.88 ± 0.06; n = 7 cells, 3 animals).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings during repetitive stimulation shown in Figure 3A-B.

claims.claim: EPSCs at SOM+ interneurons initially facilitate during trains (EPSC2 / EPSC1 = 1.78 ± 0.23).
claims.source: By contrast, the EPSCs at SOM+ interneurons initially facilitated during trains (Figure 3A & B; EPSC2 / EPSC1 = 1.78 ± 0.23; n = 8 cells, 3 animals).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings during repetitive stimulation shown in Figure 3A-B.

claims.claim: vHPC engages all three cell types, with connections at PV+ and CCK+ interneurons strong but depressing, and those at SOM+ interneurons weak but facilitating.
claims.source: These results indicate that vHPC engages all three cell types, with connections at PV+ and CCK+ interneurons strong but depressing, and those at SOM+ interneurons weak but facilitating.
claims.evidence: This is a summary inference based on the short-term plasticity data from Figure 3.

claims.claim: Stimulus trains of vHPC inputs generate decreasing AP probabilities at CCK+ interneurons (stimulus 1 and 2 AP probabilities: CCK+ = 0.97 ± 0.02 and 0.75 ± 0.06).
claims.source: We observed that stimulus trains of vHPC inputs generated decreasing AP probabilities at CCK+ and PV+ interneurons (Figure 3C & D; stimulus 1 and 2 AP probabilities: CCK+ = 0.97 ± 0.02 and 0.75 ± 0.06; n = 12 cells, 5 animals; PV+ = 0.96 ± 0.02 and 0.70 ± 0.13; n = 6 cells, 3 animals;).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by current-clamp recordings during repetitive stimulation shown in Figure 3C-D.

claims.claim: Stimulus trains of vHPC inputs generate decreasing AP probabilities at PV+ interneurons (stimulus 1 and 2 AP probabilities: PV+ = 0.96 ± 0.02 and 0.70 ± 0.13).
claims.source: We observed that stimulus trains of vHPC inputs generated decreasing AP probabilities at CCK+ and PV+ interneurons (Figure 3C & D; stimulus 1 and 2 AP probabilities: CCK+ = 0.97 ± 0.02 and 0.75 ± 0.06; n = 12 cells, 5 animals; PV+ = 0.96 ± 0.02 and 0.70 ± 0.13; n = 6 cells, 3 animals;).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by current-clamp recordings during repetitive stimulation shown in Figure 3C-D.

claims.claim: SOM+ interneurons do not fire with single pulses of vHPC inputs but are activated during trains (stimulus 1 and 2 AP probabilities: IT = 0 and 0, SOM+ = 0 and 0.57 ± 0.14).
claims.source: By contrast, although SOM+ interneurons did not fire with single pulses of vHPC inputs, they were activated during trains. Importantly, these responses were not due to recurrent network activity, as stimulation intensity was chosen here to ensure that IT cells remained quiescent (Figure 3C & D; stimulus 1 and 2 AP probabilities: IT = 0 and 0, SOM+ = 0 and 0.57 ± 0.14; n = 6 pairs, 4 animals).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by current-clamp recordings during repetitive stimulation shown in Figure 3C-D.

claims.claim: vHPC differentially engages three interneuron types with distinct dynamics during repetitive activity, with strong and depressing PV+ and CCK+ activity contributing early, and weaker but facilitating SOM+ activity contributing later.
claims.source: These findings suggest that vHPC differentially engages three interneuron types with distinct dynamics during repetitive activity, with strong and depressing PV+ and CCK+ activity contributing early, and weaker but facilitating SOM+ activity contributing later.
claims.evidence: This is a summary inference based on the data from Figure 3.

claims.claim: Labeled CCK+ cells can be rapidly and reliably activated by brief pulses of blue light, with a single AP elicited for each pulse during the train.
claims.source: Whole-cell current-clamp recordings showed that labeled cells could be rapidly and reliably activated by brief pulses of blue light, with a single AP elicited for each pulse during the train (Figure 4A; stimulus 1 to 5, AP number: 1.0 ± 0.0, n = 6 cells, 3 animals).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by current-clamp recordings shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: CCK+-evoked IPSCs are unaffected by blockers of AMPAR (10 µM NBQX) and NMDAR (10 µM CPP) but abolished by blockers of GABAAR (10 µM gabazine).
claims.source: We observed robust CCK+-evoked IPSCs, which were unaffected by blockers of AMPAR (10 µM NBQX) and NMDAR (10 µM CPP) but abolished by blockers of GABAAR (10 µM gabazine) (Figure 4B; ACSF = 97 ± 21 pA, NBQX+CPP = 97 ± 21 pA, gabazine = 0.4 ± 0.2 pA; ACSF versus NBQX + CPP, p = 0.69; NBQX + CPP versus gabazine, p = 0.01; n = 7 cells, 3 animals).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: CCK+ interneurons make inhibitory connections onto neighboring L5 pyramidal cells.
claims.source: These findings indicate that CCK+ interneurons make inhibitory connections onto neighboring L5 pyramidal cells and that our viral strategy avoids contamination from excitatory contacts due to inadvertent activation of CCK+ pyramidal cells.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the pharmacological data from Figure 4B.

claims.claim: CCK-evoked IPSCs are larger onto PT cells than IT cells (IPSC IT = 113 ± 59 pA, PT = 245 ± 79 pA, p = 0.01).
claims.source: Recording from pairs of pyramidal cells, we found that CCK-evoked IPSCs were larger onto PT cells than IT cells (Figure 4D; IPSC IT = 113 ± 59 pA, PT = 245 ± 79 pA, p = 0.01; n = 7 pairs, 4 animals).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by paired electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: CCK+ interneurons make cell-type specific connections, preferentially targeting PT cells in L5 of the IL PFC.
claims.source: These findings indicate that CCK+ interneurons make cell-type specific connections, preferentially targeting PT cells in L5 of the IL PFC.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the paired recording data from Figure 4D.

claims.claim: CCK+ inputs are highly restricted to the somatic compartment of both IT and PT cells.
claims.source: We found CCK+ inputs are highly restricted to the somatic compartment of both IT and PT cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B & D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by subcellular channelrhodopsin assisted circuit mapping (sCRACM) data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: CCK+ inputs are primarily near the soma of IT and PT cells, in contrast to the strong dendritic innervation by SOM+, 5HT3aR+, and NDNF+ cells.
claims.source: Therefore, in contrast to the strong dendritic innervation by SOM+, 5HT3aR+, and NDNF+ cells (Anastasiades et al., 2020; Marlin and Carter, 2014), these results indicate that CCK+ inputs are primarily near the soma of IT and PT cells.
claims.evidence: This is a comparison with previous literature, supported by the sCRACM data.

claims.claim: CB1R+ puncta show higher co-localization with CCK+ axons than with PV+ axons (puncta density in 103/µm2: PV+CB1R+ = 3.79 ± 0.64, GFP+CB1R+ = 11.27 ± 1.5, p=0.0003).
claims.source: We found CB1R+ puncta showed higher co-localization with CCK+ axons (based on GFP+ expression) than with PV+ axons (Figure 4E–G; puncta density in 103/µm2: PV+CB1R+ = 3.79 ± 0.64, GFP+CB1R+ = 11.27 ± 1.5, p=0.0003).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 4E-G.

claims.claim: CCK+ interneurons are enriched with presynaptic CB1Rs and are likely to undergo endocannabinoid modulation.
claims.source: These results suggest that CCK+ interneurons are enriched with presynaptic CB1Rs and are likely to undergo endocannabinoid modulation.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the immunocytochemistry data from Figure 4E-G.

claims.claim: CB1R+ puncta density is much greater at IT cells than PT cells (IT = 9.3 ± 0.5 puncta/cell, PT = 5.7 ± 0.5 puncta/cell, p<0.0001).
claims.source: While we observed CB1R+ puncta around the cell bodies of both cell types (Figure 4I), their density was much greater at IT cells (Figure 4J; IT = 9.3 ± 0.5 puncta/cell, PT = 5.7 ± 0.5 puncta/cell, p<0.0001; n = 4 animals, 247 IT cells, 207 PT cells).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 4I-J.

claims.claim: Presynaptic CB1Rs are more prominent at perisomatic connections onto IT cells, suggesting that endocannabinoid modulation may be more extensive at those projection neurons.
claims.source: These results indicate that presynaptic CB1Rs are more prominent at perisomatic connections onto IT cells, suggesting that endocannabinoid modulation may be more extensive at those projection neurons.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the immunocytochemistry data from Figure 4I-J.

claims.claim: CCK+-evoked IPSCs at IT cells undergo pronounced DSI that recovers to baseline when inputs are stimulated again 30 s later (IPSC1: before = 158 ± 34 pA, after = 91 ± 24 pA, recovery = 149 ± 33 pA; DSI ratio = 0.57 ± 0.06, p = 0.004).
claims.source: In voltage-clamp recordings from retrogradely labeled IT cells, we found that CCK+-evoked IPSCs underwent pronounced DSI that recovered to baseline when inputs were stimulated again 30 s later (Figure 5C & F; IPSC1: before = 158 ± 34 pA, after = 91 ± 24 pA, recovery = 149 ± 33 pA; DSI ratio = 0.57 ± 0.06, p = 0.004; n = 9 cells, 5 animals), with these recovery kinetics similar to previous reports in other preparations (Figure 5—figure supplement 1; n = 10 cells, four animals) (Glickfeld and Scanziani, 2006).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by DSI experiments shown in Figure 5C and F.

claims.claim: The CB1R inverse agonist 10 µM AM-251 blocks DSI at IT cells (IPSC1: before = 189 ± 53 pA, after = 168 ± 44 pA, recovery = 185 ± 55; DSI ratio = 0.92 ± 0.04, p = 0.08).
claims.source: We confirmed the involvement of endocannabinoid signaling by blocking DSI with the CB1R inverse agonist 10 µM AM-251 (Figure 5D & F; IPSC1: before = 189 ± 53 pA, after = 168 ± 44 pA, recovery = 185 ± 55; DSI ratio = 0.92 ± 0.04, p = 0.08; n = 7 cells, 4 animals).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 5D and F.

claims.claim: PV+ and SOM+-evoked IPSCs at IT cells have minimal DSI (IPSC1 DSI ratio: PV+ = 0.94 ± 0.02, p = 0.11; SOM+ = 0.87 ± 0.05, p = 0.02).
claims.source: We also confirmed this modulation was specific to CCK+ inputs, as PV+ and SOM+-evoked IPSCs at IT cells had minimal DSI (Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 2; IPSC1 DSI ratio: PV+ = 0.94 ± 0.02, p = 0.11; n = 7 cells, 3 animals; SOM+ = 0.87 ± 0.05, p = 0.02; n = 8 cells, 3 animals; PV+ versus CCK+, p = 0.0007; SOM+ versus CCK+, p = 0.008).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by DSI experiments shown in Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: There is minimal DSI at PT cells (IPSC1before = 208 ± 40 pA, after = 202 ± 44 pA, recovery = 205 ± 40 pA; DSI ratio = 0.95 ± 0.04, p = 0.22).
claims.source: Surprisingly, we found minimal DSI at PT cells, indicating modulation also strongly depends on postsynaptic cell type (Figure 5E & F; IPSC1before = 208 ± 40 pA, after = 202 ± 44 pA, recovery = 205 ± 40 pA; DSI ratio = 0.95 ± 0.04, p = 0.22; n = 7 cells, 3 animals).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by DSI experiments shown in Figure 5E and F.

claims.claim: Although CCK+ interneurons broadly contact L5 pyramidal cells, the connections undergo prominent CB1R-mediated DSI only at IT cells and not nearby PT cells.
claims.source: These findings indicate that although CCK+ interneurons broadly contact L5 pyramidal cells, the connections undergo prominent CB1R-mediated DSI only at IT cells and not nearby PT cells.
claims.evidence: This is a summary inference based on the DSI data from Figure 5.

claims.claim: Equivalent CB1R modulation of CCK+ inputs to IT cells also occurs under more physiological conditions.
claims.source: Together, these experiments indicate that equivalent CB1R modulation of CCK+ inputs to IT cells also occurs under more physiological conditions.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on current-clamp DSI experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: WIN reduces CCK+-evoked IPSCs at IT cells, which is reversed by AM-251 (baseline = 234 ± 53 pA, WIN = 106 ± 26 pA, AM-251 = 206 ± 50 pA; baseline versus WIN, p = 0.008; WIN versus AM-251, p = 0.016).
claims.source: In voltage-clamp recordings from L5 IT cells, we found that WIN reduced CCK+-evoked IPSCs, which was reversed by AM-251 (Figure 6A & C; baseline = 234 ± 53 pA, WIN = 106 ± 26 pA, AM-251 = 206 ± 50 pA; baseline versus WIN, p = 0.008; WIN versus AM-251, p = 0.016; n = 8 cells, 5 animals).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 6A and C.

claims.claim: Washing in AM-251 alone slightly increases CCK+ inputs at IT cells, confirming weak tonic CB1R activation (baseline = 186.7 ± 32 pA, AM-251 = 204.1 ± 29 pA, AM-251/baseline = 1.18 ± 0.10, p = 0.01).
claims.source: Recording at IT cells, we found that washing in AM-251 alone slightly increased the CCK+ inputs, confirming weak tonic CB1R activation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1; baseline = 186.7 ± 32 pA, AM-251 = 204.1 ± 29 pA, AM-251/baseline = 1.18 ± 0.10, p = 0.01, n = 8 cells, 5 animals).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Neither WIN nor AM-251 have any effect on CCK+-evoked IPSCs at PT cells (baseline = 292 ± 55 pA, WIN = 250 ± 36 pA, AM-251 = 281 ± 37 pA; baseline versus. WIN, p = 0.81; WIN versus AM-251, p = 0.22).
claims.source: By contrast, recordings at PT cells, we found that neither WIN nor AM-251 had any effect on CCK+-evoked IPSCs, consistent with a lack of DSI (Figure 6B & C; baseline = 292 ± 55 pA, WIN = 250 ± 36 pA, AM-251 = 281 ± 37 pA; baseline versus. WIN, p = 0.81; WIN versus AM-251, p = 0.22; n = 7 cells, 4 animals).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 6B and C.

claims.claim: The activation of CB1 receptors strongly reduces CCK+-evoked IPSCs only at IT cells but not neighboring PT cells (WIN/baseline: IT = 0.44 ± 0.05, PT = 0.92 ± 0.09, p = 0.001).
claims.source: Overall, the activation of CB1 receptors strongly reduced CCK+-evoked IPSCs only at IT cells but not neighboring PT cells (Figure 6C; WIN/baseline: IT = 0.44 ± 0.05, PT = 0.92 ± 0.09, p = 0.001).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: Wash-in of WIN increases the paired-pulse ratio (PPR) at IT cells, suggesting presynaptic modulation of release probability by CB1Rs (IPSC2 / IPSC1: baseline = 0.48 ± 0.03, WIN = 0.59 ± 0.03, AM-251 = 0.54 ± 0.02; baseline versus WIN, p = 0.03; WIN versus AM-251, p = 0.22).
claims.source: Interestingly, during trains of CCK+ stimulation, wash-in of WIN also increased the paired-pulse ratio (PPR) at IT cells, suggesting presynaptic modulation of release probability by CB1Rs (Figure 6D; IPSC2 / IPSC1: baseline = 0.48 ± 0.03, WIN = 0.59 ± 0.03, AM-251 = 0.54 ± 0.02; baseline versus WIN, p = 0.03; WIN versus AM-251, p = 0.22; n = 7 cells, 4 animals).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 6D.

claims.claim: Differences in presynaptic endocannabinoid signaling can account for the differential presence of DSI at CCK+ connections onto IT and PT cells.
claims.source: These findings demonstrate that differences in presynaptic endocannabinoid signaling can account for the differential presence of DSI at CCK+ connections onto IT and PT cells.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the pharmacological data from Figure 6.

claims.claim: Depolarization of IT cells reduces vHPC-evoked IPSCs but not EPSCs at −50 mV (before, after, recovery: IPSC1 = 102 ± 14 pA, 51 ± 10 pA, 88 ± 10 pA; EPSC1 = 248 ± 54 pA, 233 ± 48 pA, 241 ± 52 pA; DSI ratio = 0.47 ± 0.05, p = 0.02; DSE ratio = 0.99 ± 0.06, p = 0.30).
claims.source: Depolarization of IT cells (5 s to +10 mV) reduced vHPC-evoked IPSCs but not EPSCs at −50 mV (Figure 7B & E; before, after, recovery: IPSC1 = 102 ± 14 pA, 51 ± 10 pA, 88 ± 10 pA; EPSC1 = 248 ± 54 pA, 233 ± 48 pA, 241 ± 52 pA; DSI ratio = 0.47 ± 0.05, p = 0.02; DSE ratio = 0.99 ± 0.06, p = 0.30; n = 7 cells, 4 animals).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by DSI experiments with vHPC stimulation shown in Figure 7B and E.

claims.claim: There is no DSE at the vHPC to PFC connection, whereas there is prominent DSI onto IT cells.
claims.source: These findings indicate that there is no DSE at the vHPC to PFC connection, whereas there is prominent DSI onto IT cells.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the DSI/DSE data from Figure 7B and E.

claims.claim: Application of AM-251 minimizes DSI of vHPC-evoked inhibition at IT cells (IPSC1: before = 136 ± 31 pA, after = 116 ± 29 pA, recovery = 149 ± 35 pA; DSI ratio = 0.84 ± 0.03, p = 0.02; DSI in ACSF versus AM-251, p = 0.0006).
claims.source: Importantly, application of AM-251 minimized DSI, indicating that it is mediated by endocannabinoids activating CB1Rs (Figure 7C & E; IPSC1: before = 136 ± 31 pA, after = 116 ± 29 pA, recovery = 149 ± 35 pA; DSI ratio = 0.84 ± 0.03, p = 0.02; n = 7 cells, 3 animals; DSI in ACSF versus AM-251, p = 0.0006).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 7C and E.

claims.claim: Depolarization of PT cells has minimal effect on either vHPC-evoked IPSCs or EPSCs (IPSC1before = 129 ± 32 pA, after = 114 ± 27 pA, recovery = 134 ± 33 pA; DSI ratio = 0.91 ± 0.05, p = 0.10; DSE ratio = 0.89 ± 0.04, p = 0.01).
claims.source: In contrast, depolarization of PT cells had minimal effect on either vHPC-evoked IPSCs or EPSCs, confirming no DSI or DSE onto this postsynaptic cell type (Figure 7D & E; IPSC1before = 129 ± 32 pA, after = 114 ± 27 pA, recovery = 134 ± 33 pA; DSI ratio = 0.91 ± 0.05, p = 0.10; DSE ratio = 0.89 ± 0.04, p = 0.01; n = 10 cells, 4 animals).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by DSI experiments with vHPC stimulation shown in Figure 7D and E.

claims.claim: DSI of vHPC-evoked inhibition only occurs at IT cells, suggesting that CCK+ interneurons are a key node for activity-dependent modulation in communication between vHPC and PFC.
claims.source: These findings show that DSI of vHPC-evoked inhibition only occurs at IT cells, suggesting that CCK+ interneurons are a key node for activity-dependent modulation in communication between vHPC and PFC.

results.result: CCK+, PV+, and SOM+ interneurons are present in layer 5 of infralimbic PFC, with CCK+ interneurons selectively labeled using AAV-Dlx-Flex-GFP and showing minimal overlap with PV+ (11.3%) or SOM+ (6.6%) populations.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C31-C35 provide converging evidence from viral labeling, immunohistochemistry, and electrophysiology demonstrating the presence and distinct identity of CCK+ interneurons in L5 IL PFC. The use of the Dlx enhancer successfully restricted labeling to interneurons, and quantitative overlap analysis confirmed minimal co-expression with PV+ or SOM+ markers.

results.result: vHPC inputs strongly activate CCK+ and PV+ interneurons with similar EPSC amplitudes to IT cells, while SOM+ interneurons receive much weaker inputs. CCK+ and PV+ interneurons show higher action potential firing probability than IT cells in response to vHPC stimulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C36-C43 are supported by paired electrophysiological recordings comparing vHPC-evoked responses in interneurons and IT cells. The data show statistically significant differences in EPSC amplitudes (SOM+/IT ratio = 0.17, p=0.004) and AP probabilities, with appropriate controls including TTX/4-AP for monosynaptic connections and consistent light intensities within pairs.

results.result: vHPC inputs to CCK+ and PV+ interneurons exhibit short-term depression (PPR ~0.82-0.88), while inputs to SOM+ interneurons show facilitation (PPR = 1.78). During repetitive stimulation, CCK+ and PV+ interneurons show decreasing AP probability while SOM+ interneurons are recruited during trains.
results.evaluation: Claims C44-C51 demonstrate distinct short-term plasticity profiles across interneuron types using repetitive optogenetic stimulation (5 pulses at 20 Hz). The data include both voltage-clamp measurements of synaptic dynamics and current-clamp recordings of AP probability, with appropriate controls to exclude recurrent network activity for SOM+ activation.

results.result: CCK+ interneurons make functional inhibitory connections onto L5 pyramidal cells, with stronger connections onto PT cells (245 ± 79 pA) than IT cells (113 ± 59 pA, p=0.01).
results.evaluation: Claims C52-C56 are supported by optogenetic activation of CCK+ interneurons combined with pharmacological validation (gabazine abolishes responses while NBQX+CPP do not) and paired recordings from retrogradely labeled IT and PT cells. The cell-type specificity is statistically significant and consistent with previous findings for other interneuron types.

results.result: CCK+ interneurons target the somatic compartment of both IT and PT cells, as demonstrated by subcellular channelrhodopsin-assisted circuit mapping (sCRACM).
results.evaluation: Claims C57-C58 are supported by sCRACM experiments using a 10×10 grid of light stimulation across the somato-dendritic axis. The data show restricted perisomatic targeting, contrasting with dendritic targeting by other interneuron types. The methodology is appropriate with TTX/4-AP to isolate monosynaptic inputs.

results.result: CB1R+ puncta show higher co-localization with CCK+ axons than PV+ axons (11.27 vs 3.79 per 10³/µm², p=0.0003), and CB1R+ puncta density is greater around IT cells (9.3 ± 0.5) than PT cells (5.7 ± 0.5, p<0.0001).
results.evaluation: Claims C59-C62 are supported by quantitative immunocytochemistry with appropriate statistical analysis. The differential CB1R expression on CCK+ vs PV+ axons and around IT vs PT cell bodies provides anatomical evidence for cell-type-specific endocannabinoid modulation. Sample sizes are adequate (247 IT cells, 207 PT cells from 4 animals).

results.result: CCK+-evoked IPSCs at IT cells undergo pronounced CB1R-mediated DSI (DSI ratio = 0.57 ± 0.06, p=0.004), which is blocked by AM-251 and specific to CCK+ inputs. PT cells show minimal DSI (DSI ratio = 0.95 ± 0.04, p=0.22).
results.evaluation: Claims C63-C67 demonstrate cell-type-specific DSI using a standard depolarization protocol with appropriate controls including AM-251 blockade and comparison to PV+ and SOM+ inputs. The recovery kinetics match previous reports, and the lack of DSI at PT cells is statistically validated. The low-Cl⁻ internal solution and recording at -50 mV are appropriate methodological choices.

results.result: CB1R modulation of CCK+ inputs to IT cells occurs under physiological conditions in current-clamp recordings.
results.evaluation: Claim C68 is supported by current-clamp DSI experiments (Figure 5—figure supplement 3) that account for membrane potential changes after AP firing. The experiments include appropriate controls for voltage-dependent effects and AM-251 blockade, demonstrating that the modulation is not an artifact of voltage-clamp conditions.

results.result: Direct activation of CB1 receptors with WIN reduces CCK+-evoked IPSCs at IT cells (WIN/baseline = 0.44 ± 0.05) but not PT cells (0.92 ± 0.09, p=0.001), with increased paired-pulse ratio suggesting presynaptic modulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C69-C74 provide pharmacological evidence for presynaptic CB1R-mediated modulation using WIN and AM-251. The cell-type specificity matches the DSI results, and the PPR increase supports a presynaptic mechanism. The detection of weak tonic CB1R activation with AM-251 alone adds supporting evidence. Statistical comparisons are appropriate.

results.result: vHPC-evoked feed-forward inhibition undergoes CB1R-mediated DSI selectively at IT cells (DSI ratio = 0.47 ± 0.05, p=0.02) but not PT cells (0.91 ± 0.05, p=0.10), with no DSE at either cell type.
results.evaluation: Claims C75-C79 demonstrate that endocannabinoid modulation of vHPC-evoked inhibition recapitulates the properties of direct CCK+ stimulation. The experiments appropriately measure both EPSCs and IPSCs at -50 mV, showing selective DSI without DSE. AM-251 blockade confirms CB1R involvement. This result integrates the circuit-level findings.

results.result: vHPC inputs evoke both EPSCs (386 ± 49 pA) and IPSCs (961 ± 207 pA) at IT cells with an E/I ratio of 0.50 ± 0.08, indicating robust feed-forward inhibition.
results.evaluation: Claims C28-C30 provide initial characterization of vHPC-evoked responses using voltage-clamp recordings at different holding potentials. The methodology is standard and the E/I ratio calculation is appropriate. This establishes the motivation for identifying the interneurons responsible for feed-forward inhibition.

results.result: The study demonstrates that vHPC strongly activates CB1R-expressing CCK+ interneurons that participate in feed-forward inhibition, with CCK+ connections undergoing CB1R-mediated DSI selectively at IT cells, and vHPC-evoked inhibition showing the same cell-type-specific modulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C83-C86 are summary statements that accurately reflect the major findings of the manuscript. These conclusions are well-supported by the convergent evidence from connectivity, pharmacology, and DSI experiments presented throughout the results section.

results.result: The introduction establishes the functional importance of vHPC-PFC connections, the role of PV+, SOM+, and CCK+ interneurons in cortical inhibition, and the technical challenges in studying CCK+ interneurons that are overcome by intersectional viral approaches.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C27 provide appropriate background context supported by citations to previous literature. The claims about CCK+ interneuron properties (CB1R expression, DSI mechanism) are well-established in the field, and the technical limitations of CCK-Cre mice and solutions using Dlx enhancers are accurately described.

results.result: The discussion contextualizes findings within the broader literature on PFC interneuron diversity, vHPC connectivity, and CCK+ interneuron function, noting that CCK+ interneurons are enriched in PFC and positioned to mediate feed-forward inhibition from vHPC.
results.evaluation: Claims C87-C100 appropriately discuss the findings in relation to previous work, including comparisons to other cortical regions and the hippocampus. The interpretations are generally well-supported by citations, though some statements involve speculation about functional implications that would require additional experiments to fully validate.

results.result: The discussion notes that CCK+ connections preferentially target PT cells (similar to other interneuron types) and target the soma of both IT and PT cells, which may explain the lack of asynchronous release compared to hippocampal CCK+ synapses.
results.evaluation: Claims C101-C106 appropriately integrate current findings with previous work on biased inhibition and subcellular targeting. The comparison to hippocampal CCK+ synapses and the inference about asynchronous release is reasonable given the sCRACM data, though direct measurements of asynchronous release were not presented.

results.result: The discussion proposes that cell-type-specific endocannabinoid modulation may involve differential CB1R organization at boutons or contributions from multiple CCK+ interneuron subtypes, drawing parallels to mechanisms described in hippocampus and amygdala.
results.evaluation: Claims C107-C113 present reasonable mechanistic hypotheses for the observed cell-type specificity, but these remain speculative. The nanoscale organization hypothesis (C111) and the possibility of multiple CCK+ subtypes (C113) are plausible based on literature, but the current data cannot distinguish between these mechanisms. Additional experiments would be needed to test these hypotheses.

results.result: The discussion proposes that endocannabinoid-mediated disinhibition at IT cells could increase the E/I ratio, promote local PFC processing, enhance vHPC-PFC synchrony during behavior, and shift PFC output toward intratelencephalic targets.
results.evaluation: Claims C114-C119 present reasonable functional hypotheses about the behavioral implications of the findings, but these remain speculative. While the inference about increased E/I ratio (C116) follows logically from the data, the proposed effects on behavior (C117-C119) would require in vivo experiments to validate. These are appropriate directions for future work but are not directly supported by the current data.

results.result: The discussion concludes that endocannabinoids influence vHPC-PFC communication by selectively modulating CCK+ to IT cell connections, with potential implications for cognition, emotion, and mental health disorders.
results.evaluation: Claims C120-C122 appropriately summarize the main finding (C122) and place it in the context of established roles for endocannabinoid signaling in behavior and disease (C120-C121). While the behavioral and clinical implications remain to be tested, the core conclusion about selective modulation of CCK+ to IT connections is well-supported by the data.
